newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA BACK ON TRACK WITH WIN OVER LUXEMBOURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA BACK ON TRACK WITH WIN OVER LUXEMBOURG.

text.p: Russia got their World Cup campaign back on course on Wednesday with a comfortable 3-0 win over Luxembourg that will help erase memories of last month's 1-1 draw in Cyprus.
The Russians never managed to find top gear but were content to secure three points against a Luxembourg side reduced to 10 men for the final half hour.
Metz defender Jeff Strasser was sent off for dangerous play as he tried to prevent Igor Simutenkov making a pass inside the area that let Sergei Grishin in for Russia's second goal.
A minute later Reggiana striker Simutenkov had a free header from a long through ball to make it 3-0. Valery Kechinov had scored the first after 20 minutes.
The result left Russia in second place in group five with 11 points from five games. They are two points behind Israel who beat Cyprus 2-0 at home on Wednesday.
But the Israelis, who travel to Moscow on June 8, have played a game more.
Russian coach Boris Ignatyev said he was "satisfied" with the result which kept his side's chances of qualification solid.

He praised the young domestic players he brought into the side, singling out Grishin. The 23-year-old Dynamo Moscow player was sent on for Racing Santander striker Vladimir Beschastnykh, whom Ignatyev accused of lacking commitment.

The Russians may well see out their campaign for France '98 without the services of stalwart Roma defender Omari Tetradze. Doctors said he could be out for up to six months after tearing ligaments in an awkward fall in the first half.
